newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE BRENT LOCKED IN UPTREND, MAY RIDE IRAQ.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE BRENT LOCKED IN UPTREND, MAY RIDE IRAQ.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* $19 will be tested on Brent (September chart) and it will probably hold but $19.60 resistance may prove difficult to clear. * Parallel uptrend lines on the spot month continuation chart for Brent stemming from the June 11 trough of $17.32 and the high of $17.90 from the same day continue to cap and underpin Brent prices locking the market in long term uptrend.

Good trendline support may continue to sustain the long term uptrend for IPE Brent futures against the pressure of Iraqi crude sales while gas oil strength may stall for a while with the market due for a correction, analysts said.
Independent analyst, Elli Gifford said "$19 will be tested on Brent (September chart) and it will probably hold though resistance at the $19.60 double top may prove difficult to clear".
She said the market was looking overbought and due for a correction but thought that the $19.60 barrier would be cleared eventually setting the market to trade just below $20.

Parallel uptrend lines on the spot month continuation chart for Brent stemming from the June 11 trough of $17.32 and the high of $17.90 from the same day continue to cap and underpin Brent prices whilst locking the market in long term uptrend, analysts said.

The market has broken above trendline resistance, that starts from the June 11 high of $17.90 and passes through July 17 $18.79 high, over the past three trading days and Wednesday's Iraq crude sales related sell-off found support at $19.10 on this line.

Analysts said this trendline should offer some resistance at around $19.30 today and this combined with the markets fundamental nervousness should stall the rally for a while, but that it looks set to continue once the fundamental pressures have passed.

Several attractive targets remain in focus with May 27's $19.88 and May 16's $20.60, where a rally similar to current one failed, but previous attempts to break out of this up channel have proven short term and the market has corrected back into line.

On the September chart prices remain underscored by an uptrend support line stemming from July 21's $18.00 low, but there is little resistance to the upside until the double top of $20.40 from May 16 and May 20 once the $19.60 double top from earlier this week is passed.
Slow stochastics lines have crossed three times this week at a bearishly high level, but sturdy support today at about $19.00-$19.10 could keep the market on course for higher ground.
Gas oil's bullish gap higher on the spot month chart from Monday's $173.50 high and Tuesday's $175 low remains intact and supportive despite a dip to $174.25 on Wednesday.
Analysts said this could provide base for the market to take another step higher with May 22 $179.50 the next upside target.
But some thought a correction lower was more likely with the market looking overbought.
Elli Gifford was more bearish in the near term for gas oil, "The market is even more overbought than crude and the $173.50 support level could be tested and go today".
She pegged resistance around Wednesday's high but said this was unlikely to be tested today.
Wednesday's price action completed an engulfing pattern on the spot month chart adding to the bearish undertone.

This occurs on candlestick charts when a white real body (the range between the sessions open and close which, if white, means the close was higher than the low and the opposite if the real body is black) is engulfed by a black real body formed in the next session.
This is seen by those who follow Japanese candlestick charting techniques as a signal for a top reversal where the bears have taken over from the bulls in an uptrending market.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
